topic: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max): the index score, the open weights, and the machine that fits them
title: DeepSeek Flash 1017 costs 26 cents a task, and 128 GB to run it
description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 landed with MIT weights and a top open-weight index score. What it costs per benchmark task, and which machine actually loads it. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: DeepSeek's Flash costs twenty-six cents a benchmark task.
Your card still can't run DeepSeek's new open weights.
Forty-five on the index, and the weights are already yours.
Seven hundred sixty-three billion parameters, free to download today.
DeepSeek 1017 is open, MIT licensed, and huge.
The best open model just got too big for your card.

Second of one hundred twenty-one open models. Not first.
Open weights day one. Your gaming card day never.
narration_full: DeepSeek's Flash costs twenty-six cents a benchmark task. One task on the Artificial Analysis index, an independent scoreboard. The size will surprise you: five hundred fifty-two billion parameters. It's a mixture of experts, a receptionist waking the few each word needs. Sixteen billion wake per word. She re-picks for every word. The weights are MIT licensed, downloadable today. A community converter reports a build fitting one DGX Spark with one hundred twenty-eight gigabytes of shared memory. Flash is a name, not a size. Your twenty-four-gigabyte card stays out, at any quant, any shrunken file. What's yours is the number: twenty-six cents a task, no new box.
